rationale: Across the seminal discovery publications establishing FILIP1-related neuromuscular disorder with dysmorphic facies (OMIM #620775)—specifically Schnabel et al. (2023) and Roos et al. (2023), which are indexed as the definitive references in the neuromuscular gene tables—exactly 10 affected individuals were reported in detail (5 in Schnabel et al. from 3 families, and 5 in Roos et al. from 4 families). In both foundational cohorts, dysmorphic facial features and neuromuscular involvement (muscle weakness, hypotonia, and myopathology) were reported across all assessed individuals (10/10, 100%). Although recent exome cohort screenings (e.g., Chaurasia et al., 2026) report further identification of individuals with biallelic FILIP1 variants in syndromic arthrogryposis cohorts, the initial seminal discovery cohort establishing the phenotype consists precisely of these 10 individuals.

evidence.text: Schnabel et al. (2023) reported five affected individuals from three independent families with homozygous truncating variants in FILIP1 presenting with congenital contractures, scoliosis, microcephaly, and facial dysmorphism.

source.title: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 cause autosomal recessive arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with microcephaly
source.quote: Here, we report five affected individuals from three independent families sharing an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee and foot as well as scoliosis, reduced palmar and plantar skin folds, microcephaly and facial dysmorphism.

evidence.text: Roos et al. (2023) described five patients from four unrelated consanguineous families harboring homozygous FILIP1 variants (two nonsense and two missense), all exhibiting neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness, myopathology, and dysmorphic features.

source.title: Bi-allelic variants of FILIP1 cause congenital myopathy, dysmorphism and neurological defects
source.quote: Here, we report on five patients from four unrelated consanguineous families with homozygous FILIP1 variants (two nonsense and two missense)... Patients exhibit a broad spectrum of neurological symptoms including brain malformations, neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness and pathology and dysmorphic features.

evidence.text: The international neuromuscular disorders nuclear gene table (2025/2026) indexes congenital neuromuscular disorder with dysmorphic facies (NMDF, OMIM #620775) under autosomal recessive inheritance caused by FILIP1 variants, citing Schnabel et al. (2023) and Roos et al. (2023) as the seminal foundational papers.

evidence.text: Chaurasia et al. (2026) reported that systematic copy number loss screening and collaboration identified additional affected individuals with biallelic FILIP1 variants presenting with syndromic arthrogryposis, indicating that the global patient cohort is expanding beyond the initial discovery series.

source.title: Systematic analysis of homozygous autosomal copy number losses in exomes improves diagnostic yield and uncovers ultra-rare recessive disorders
source.quote: Further analysis of the data and identification of additional affected individuals through collaboration led to identification of biallelic FILIP1 and FAM177A1 variants as causes of a syndromic arthrogryposis and a neuromuscular disorder respectively.

new_directions.question_text: How do clinical penetrance and contracture severity compare between homozygous truncating loss-of-function variants and homozygous missense variants in expanded cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Schnabel et al. reported purely truncating variants with severe contractures and microcephaly, whereas Roos et al. included missense variants (such as p.Pro1133Leu) that highlighted myofibrillar core-like disintegration and filamin-C accumulation. Clarifying variant-specific severity will aid phenotypic differentiation.

new_directions.question_text: What specific dysmorphic facial features reliably discriminate FILIP1-related neuromuscular disorder from classic congenital myopathies and distal arthrogryposes (e.g., RYR1-, FLNC-, or MYH3-related conditions)?
new_directions.rationale: While 100% of the core discovery individuals exhibited dysmorphic features, defining the exact facial gestalt and distinguishing features against overlapping arthrogryposis multiplex congenita conditions is needed for bedside classification.
